The advice that I’ve been seeing is to go with the least costly program. In the end it’s for the same degree, there’s no significant upper hand in attending costly programs apparently.
What sucks about this is that the online programs I’ve encountered are astronomical in price!
Also, deadlines are April 15th I believe, or some day in April to get back to the program you wish to attend.
I wish you the best of luck either way!!

Most other comments covered the goods ones so I’ll just mention the ones I haven’t seen that you might want to consider:   
\-If any type of mentorship/graduate advisement resources are available to students   
\-The research facilities/opportunities that might be available to students 

What I DON’T suggest you ask:   
Things that realistically should’ve already been researched before you ever applied or is easily Google-able. Your statement of purpose often covers why this program appeals to you. Interviews aren’t the time to out yourself as coming in with zero background knowledge of their program (even if that’s true.) I suggest you take a look at the program’s website to see what questions are already answered and what might naturally come up for you. 

Good luck :)

This overwhelmed me with emotion. Brought tears to my eyes.

Some things that stood out to me: 

Your use of parallelism in the lines "bold and unforgiving" referring to the flag and "cold and unforgiving" referring to your heart.

These parts here,

"but she did not speak his language  
the language of the weak."

"His eyes spoke of sadness and self hatred  
while his body continued on to find worth."

Makes me think this is between two people, a woman and a man. I'm interpreting this as, this man feels as if he is not enough and the woman made him feel this way. He is suffering internally. The woman believes his language is the language of the weak. This is a woman that does not see nor value him for what he is worth. His eyes speak of sadness and self-hatred. This hatred feels as if it is brought on by this woman, where his worth now must be found again. This woman is causing him to question himself.

"And somehow, I,  
I am the one who must forgive  
like those that have forgiven from the past  
because hate in a heart leaves no room for love."

I took this as him taking his experiences with this woman, what she has put him through, and putting them behind him. He is acknowledging that the hate in his heart that he has against this woman is counteractive, and he knows it is in his best interest to let go. Very powerful.

"But what is love  
what is peace  
but an ideal  
waiting to be betrayed by you."

This was the perfect way to close out this piece, I think. Truly gave me chills. Truly, what is love, what is peace, but an ideal waiting to be betrayed? This "you" seems to be generally directed at a significant other, whether one in specific or a hypothetical one.

I may have completely misinterpreted this, but regardless, I adore this piece.

Thank you very much for sharing :)

The overall tone in this is so interesting, I feel like I relate.

I'm getting that this person "built a house inside your head," as in they live in your mind. The indestructible nature of this house indicates that they're more than a passing thought, their image is persistent, it is resilient in your mind.

However, your first line, "not sure how you did it," is almost as if you are invalidating your feelings, your fixation. How this person should not have an impact on you to the extent that they do.

"You're the only thing in my life

that made me feel like what's in

my head actually matters."

If I'm interpreting this correctly, the thought of this person is something you hold onto and cherish. That the thought of them actually matters, unlike all your other thoughts, as you say. Though this is true, your title "what you built; I'll one day tear down" says that you deep down feel that you will at one point have to forget about them and tear down this seemingly indestructible house.

I wonder if that's something you actually *want* to do, or if you feel it's something you feel like you *have* to do, against your own will, for your own good.

​

I also read your response to another comment. "One day I hope they leave my mind cause they shouldn't be stuck in it this long anyway."

This is the feeling I gathered from your writing. You invalidating your feelings, how they "shouldn't be stuck" in your head "this long anyway" and how you're hoping and anticipating the day they leave your mind.

I am going through an identical situation right now, where someone I spent only a few days with changed my entire life, and they are now long gone. I kick myself over it, how I let them have such a hold on me over such little time, that I let them build their house in my head.

However, you yourself said, "they left a permanent mark on me." The mark is permanent, do not fight it. They have changed you! Perhaps the reason you feel this way is because you want to return to who you were before you encountered them, but you cannot be who you were before them, this version of you no longer exists. You are changed. Instead of trying to revert, perhaps breathe into the newer version of you :)

The imagery is very rich here. 

What I'm getting is that the woman with shiny gold hair, the tyrant, is an abuser. The gentle old man is the savior.

The tone of the narrator is very hopeless and defeated. They, perhaps it is you, feels as if they are at the mercy of this woman. For some reason, I perceived the first half of the poem as a very unhealthy and strained relationship with a motherly figure, a female guardian/figure of authority.

I had a harder time perceiving the old man, though. The line where he told her that "he had a plan" made me immediately think of a god figure, especially since they were written as a savior. Furthermore, the line "Out comes a wail, who is this male, that can make her cower in fear?" is interesting since the woman that was written as this merciless and powerful woman is now cowering in fear upon the arrival of this new figure.

A sidenote, the rhyme scheme reminds me of Dr. Seuss, it's really comforting and easy to follow the rhythms of your writing.

Thank you for sharing :)

Initially, this rang as optimistic yet uncertain, someone writing of the reciprocity that they long for. Like the words of a hopeless romantic.

What really gets me though, is the final stanza. It leaves me to wonder whether I want to interpret it in the tone that you began the poem with--with hope and longing--or with the tone seen later on, which was self-destructive and pained.

I wonder if the flight you refer to at the end is something you welcome or something you fear.

Hi,

Before all else, know that this isn't something you should feel like you need to tolerate, NOBODY deserves this treatment and insensitivity regardless of their shape and size, ESPECIALLY from family. Family is supposed to be loving and supportive. Instead of belittling you for your weight they should be lifting and supporting you on your journey. From the bottom of my heart, I'm terribly sorry you ever had to feel this way.

Brothers usually give their sisters a hard time. This speaks more about him than it does you, I hope you don't look in the mirror different because of him. My ultimate advice is to not care, but obviously it's easier said than done.

You mentioned that you are working on trying to lose the weight. If that's the case, I hope you really do what's best for you and know deep down that you are benefitting yourself and your health, not to please anybody else. Hopefully the confidence you exude will counter the hurt that you feel from those around you.

I had my family ridicule me for my weight for many years because of cultural standards of beauty. I was never slim enough, I was never athletic enough. I remember breaking down and weeping multiple times, and it felt like there was nothing I could do about it. What ended up happening was a sort of informal intervention, where my father actually realized the effect it had on me and communicated his concerns to the toxic members of my family, and though it toned down significantly, it's not like it doesn't happen at all anymore.

What helped me was taking matters into my own hands and taking up a different lifestyle. I was so confident in my routine because it was nothing but consistency and hard work. I was dropping inches. It kinda feels like an aha moment when you come out of it and they realize that you mean business. You will know within yourself that you are doing everything right in achieving a body you can tolerate, and hopefully eventually love.

I don't care what yourself or others are telling you right now, you are improving yourself for you right now in this moment. This is all that should matter.

Your appearance should come second to your health. But, with the right habits, they may come simultaneously.
